drivers.description: Lord of the Rings, The (5.01 Spanish)

Unlike the German, French and Italian releases, which share their English sibling's CPU ROM byte for byte, its CPU game ROM is its own, shared with no English release. The switch matrix, lamp matrix, coil complement and playfield hardware are unchanged. Against the root driver it differs in the CPU game ROM (lotrcpul.501 against the root's lotrcpua.a00), the display ROM (lotrdspl.501 against lotrdspa.a00) and the whole five-ROM sound set (LOTR_SND_SP against LOTR_SND).

mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest in the under-playfield trough on printed switches 11, 12 and 13 with the fourth position read by opto 14, the 4-Ball Trough VUK Opto at the eject end. Solenoid 1, the Trough Up-Kicker, lifts the ball at the eject end into the shooter lane, where switch 16 reads it. Printed switch 15, the 4-Ball Stacking Opto, watches the stack feeding the trough. The manual numbers the positions from the left, so printed Trough #1 is the position furthest from the shooter lane; the retained VPW script numbers its trough objects in the opposite order, which is a labelling difference and not a wiring disagreement. All three retained scripts initialise switches 11-14 closed at start of game because balls rest on them.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough and up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: The Balrog toy is driven by motor 041-5088-01 on printed solenoid 22, gated by the DC relay 520-5066-00 on printed solenoid 20. Printed switches 31 Balrog Open and 32 Balrog Closed read the two end positions and are mutually exclusive; the retained VPW script asserts one and clears the other as the motor runs. Printed switch 28 Balrog Hit is a separate above-playfield switch on the toy that registers a ball strike and is driven in the retained script from a wobble value rather than from the motor position, so a recreation must not derive it from the open or closed state.

mechanisms.behavior: The One Ring on the back panel is held and released by the magnet on printed solenoid 6, which is the only output with its own fuse, printed F20 4A 250v slow-blow and marked THIS GAME ONLY in the quick reference fuse chart. Printed opto 47 Ring Made, on the back panel, reads a ball completing the ring. Printed solenoid 26 flashes the ring and 27 the back panel behind it.
mechanisms.label: One Ring magnet and back panel

mechanisms.behavior: Printed solenoid 8, the Loop Diverter, steers a ball out of the loop toward the left Orthanc tower. The manual carries a dedicated Diverter Gate Adjustment Procedure: with power off and the playfield raised, the crank-bar set screw is loosened, the paddle is held against the right flat rail to open the gate to the left tower, the plunger is pushed home, and the screw is retightened so the paddle rests as close to the left flat rail as possible without touching it. Printed switch 42 Inner Loop and the orbit switches 20, 21, 37 and 38 read balls through the loop.
mechanisms.label: Loop diverter gate

mechanisms.behavior: Three vertical up-kickers and one saucer return balls to play. Printed solenoid 3 with switch 9 is the left VUK, printed solenoid 4 with opto 41 is the top VUK, printed solenoid 5 with switch 30 is the right VUK, and printed solenoid 19 with switch 46 is the top saucer. The retained VPW and JPSalas scripts label solenoid 4 Upper-Left VUK and solenoid 19 Upper-Right Kicker; the manual's Top VUK and Top Saucer are the printed names and control.
mechanisms.label: Vertical up-kickers and top saucer

positions.description: Top vertical up-kicker, read by an opto.
positions.label: Top VUK

mechanisms.behavior: A separate mini playfield carries four switches printed Mini PF U.L., U.R., L.L. and L.R. at addresses 33 to 36, all switch part 180-5057-00. The printed switch-location drawing shows the mini playfield moved off the main playfield for clarity, so its printed drawing position is not its installed position; the coordinates here come from the retained recreations.
mechanisms.label: Mini playfield

mechanisms.behavior: UK cabinets add three up and down posts driven from a UK 3X Transformer Driver Board and exposed on Whitestar auxiliary outputs 33, 34 and 35. The cabinet wiring page names them the Post Save feature: the left of the two UK-only cabinet buttons (printed switch 1) raises the Left Outlane Ball Deflector (Aux 1), the right button (switch 8) the Right Outlane Ball Deflector (Aux 3), and both together the Center Up/Down Post between the flippers (Aux 2). The printed coil and flash lamp location drawing prints Aux 1 and Aux 3 at the tops of the outlanes and Aux 2 between the flippers. These are absent from non-UK cabinets, as are the two cabinet-side buttons.
mechanisms.label: UK-only up/down posts

PinMAME exposes Whitestar's general-illumination relay as a single aggregate channel. The cabinet itself has four separately fused 5.7v AC illumination circuits behind the one relay, printed F24 (circuit 1, BRN-WHT, back panel), F25 (circuit 2, YEL, lower playfield and two spotlights), F26 (circuit 3, GRN, upper middle playfield and coin door) and F27 (circuit 4, VIO, upper playfield), so a recreation must not infer four controllable channels from the fuse chart. The G.I. wiring diagram (PDF 121), the transformer's parts listing (010-5012-01, 'Transformer 5.7v AC') and the cabinet wiring print the G.I. supply as 5.7v AC; only the quick-reference fuse chart prints 6.3v AC for F24-F27, so the nominal voltage follows the three agreeing pages. The 2022 manual's G.I. wiring diagram (PDF 121) draws 22 playfield sockets on its bottom view: 7 yellow, 5 green and 10 violet. Its circuit table prints the green circuit as Upper Middle Playfield X2 where the drawing has five green sockets, and every retained recreation carries a G.I. light at the three green sockets along the left side, so the drawing's five are placed; the page's footnote says bulb quantities may change during production. The two #555 spotlights above the playfield sit in light reflectors on the return-lane plastics, placed at the reflector leaders of the playfield parts drawing (PDF 83). The eight back-panel bulbs stand in a row along the top of the upright back panel: PDF 121's rear-view inset of the panel draws them, mapped along the panel through its six mode-lamp sockets and the One Ring, and placed on the panel's plane like the mode lamps 73-78; the back panel's exploded front view (PDF 112) draws the same row and agrees within 0.004 for every socket. The two coin-door bulbs (three on European doors) are on this channel too but are cabinet hardware and not placed. Quantity counts every bulb on a US machine.
